related_questions.question: What's happening with student loans on May 5th?

text_blocks.snippet: On May 5, 2025, the US Department of Education will resume collecting on defaulted federal student loans for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic began in March 2020. This means that borrowers in default will face potential consequences like wage garnishment and offset of federal payments such as tax refunds. The Department of Education is also relaunching an enhanced Income-Driven Repayment (IDR) process to simplify enrollment.

list.title: Enhanced IDR Process:
list.snippet: The DOE is streamlining the IDR process to make it easier for borrowers to enroll and recertify their income.

list.title: Potential Consequences:

list.title: Increased Scrutiny:
